anti_overlap: Does NOT cover sensor fusion for routing (fd-kalman-filter-fusion)
Does NOT cover queueing/scheduling under load (fd-queueing-priority-scheduling)
decision_lens: Does this orchestration step plan over a rolling horizon with anticipated cost, or does it react only after the budget breach?
distance_rationale: MPC is taught in chemical engineering and aerospace, almost never in LLM platform engineering, despite the same fundamental problem (constrained optimization under prediction uncertainty)
expected_isomorphisms: Prediction horizon maps to multi-turn token forecast; constraint set maps to budget gates; receding-horizon update maps to per-turn replan; feedforward-cost maps to pre-flight budget check
focus: Reviews sprint pacing, budget gates, and hook firing through the lens of Model Predictive Control — rolling-horizon optimization with explicit constraints
name: fd-mpc-control-budget
persona: Apply the perspective of a control engineer running an MPC controller — they care about prediction horizon, the constraint set, control effort, the receding-horizon update, and the difference between feedforward (anticipated) and feedback (reactive) corrections
review_areas: Prediction horizon: do /sprint /work loops estimate token spend for the next 3-5 steps, or only check budget after each step?
Constraint set: are budget constraints (cache TTL, MEMORY.md size, /loop interval) explicit in a single state object, or scattered across hooks?
Control effort minimization: when budget is tight, does the orchestrator pick cheaper agents (Sonnet, smaller subagent prompts), or always default to the same dispatch?
Receding-horizon update: each turn replans — is plan persisted across turns, or restarted each time?
Feedforward vs feedback: when a known-expensive operation is queued (e.g., /flux-review with 16 agents), is upstream budget pre-checked?
Disturbance rejection: unexpected interruptions (user redirect, hook fire, MCP disconnect) — does orchestration replan gracefully?

severity_examples.condition: User sees budget warning mid-sprint with no graceful degradation path
severity_examples.scenario: /sprint runs to budget exhaustion on C4 epics because there is no horizon-aware planner that anticipates cumulative spend across phases

severity_examples.condition: Replan cost duplicates orientation work the previous turn already did
severity_examples.scenario: Each turn replans from scratch instead of carrying a running plan with confidence intervals

severity_examples.condition: Budget breach mid-pipeline; partial results, no clean rollback
severity_examples.scenario: Heavy operations (/flux-review at 400kt) are dispatched without pre-checking remaining session budget

source_domain: Model Predictive Control (process industries, autonomous vehicles)
success_hints: Sketch a horizon-N planning loop for /sprint or /work
Identify the constraint state object (current cost, remaining budget, expected steps)
Recommend feedforward-cost estimates for the 3-5 most expensive primitives
Reference receding-horizon explicitly when proposing replans
task_context: Sylveste's sprint and /work loops have budget feedback (sylveste-ynh7 saved 2,285 tok/session post-hoc), but most decisions are reactive — budget gates trip after spending. Apply MPC: predict budget consumption N steps ahead, plan tool calls to stay within constraints, replan each step. Identify decisions that should plan over a horizon: when to invoke heavy agents, when to defer to next session, when to compress before vs after a heavy tool call.
